tldr.text: SPY -0.08%, QQQ -0.43%, SOXX -2.49%, XLK -1.08%, IGV +1.19% on Monday May 18, 2026; a modestly risk-off tape with semis, AI compute, WFE, memory, and packaging sold while software was bid.
MU closed -8.30% on softer DRAM/HBM price checks and chatter on push-outs to GPU-memory orders; sell-side and industry checks flagged weaker 2H26 pricing.
VRT closed -9.99% on heavy liquidation in AI power/cooling; no company-specific headline, just de-rating and positioning unwind.
NOW closed +8.26% on strong buy interest tied to GenAI "Now Assist" traction and platform-layer workflow demand.
ZS closed +8.53% on zero-trust / secure access positioning and AI-enhanced threat detection commentary.
AMAT closed -6.01% on follow-through selling after earnings digestion and a China export-control overhang on WFE.
NVDA closed -2.27% on de-risking ahead of Wednesday earnings, with position-squaring across the AI stack.
RBLX closed +8.98% as a standout internet momentum bid, with no single official catalyst cited in the tape.

watch_tomorrow.text: NVDA earnings and guidance will drive AI compute, memory, packaging, and WFE sentiment.
Watch whether Monday’s semi-led selloff in SOXX, XLK, and QQQ extends or stabilizes.
MU, RMBS, AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC may react first to NVDA and any HBM commentary.
VRT, ETN, DELL, SMCI, and ANET remain vulnerable to any post-NVDA de-risking.
NOW, ZS, CRWD, MDB, and SNOW can keep leading if the market continues to favor software rotation.
AEHR, NVTS, WOLF, ON, and STM need evidence that the recent de-risking was only positioning.
